correctness.rationale: The signed coefficient parameterization on Lip_0(X) is complete (the basepoint coefficient fixes the affine sum). For i in cluster j, the 1-Lipschitz distance potential yields A_ji=1-w_j+t_j(w_j-c_i); its cluster average is 1-beta_j*w_j, so K(c)>=max_j(1-beta_j*w_j)>=D=1-1/H. The positive weights c_i=1/(H beta_j m_j) attain K=D by the triangle inequality. If K=D, each beta_j*w_j=1/H and all A_ji equal their upper bound, forcing every c_i=w_j/m_j since t_j>0. This proves rigidity among arbitrary signed operators, not just symmetric ones. For R<=D the full norm optimum is unique; R>D has a relatively open affine family K<R. Includes singleton clusters, t_j=1, R=1/2. Independent small exact profiles and inspected signed-spanning-tree checker are finite corroboration only.
